fidelity_summary: Déf. 7 is faithful: it is defined for all pairs, and for non-antipodal pairs it is literally s([M, M']), independent of the representatives. Déf. 8 is correctly unmarked: both readings are formalized, and the ∪ reading is proved equivalent to the unambiguous segment form, while the Minkowski reading is proved to contradict it. Déf. 9 and Déf. 11 are marked, and the marks are earned: their content is the same class under every reading of Déf. 8 on the table, proved by three iff lemmas, so their independence from OQ-24 is a theorem, not a convention. The scan confirms the printed '+' next to a printed '∪' on the same page.
questions_for_author: OQ-24: rule « F(k) + {O} » = F(k) ∪ {O}? The evidence is four-fold. The segment sentence is equivalent to it (isConvexPart_iff_isSegConvex). The Minkowski reading contradicts that sentence on S(E) and on every nonzero linear subvariety. The Minkowski reading makes Déf. 10's « convexes contenant l » empty (issue 1). And the print uses ∪ elsewhere on the same page, so '+' is notation or a misprint. Once ruled, Déf. 8 can be marked with no code change.

Keep Déf. 9 and Déf. 11 marked before OQ-24 is ruled? Their reading-independence is proved, so the auditor finds the marks earned; holding them with Déf. 8 would be a policy choice, not a mathematical one.
